title: ChatGPT 推出面向日常对话优化的 GPT-6.2 Sol
content:
我们正在 Chat 标签页中推出一版 GPT-6.2 Sol，针对日常对话进行了优化。
它在处理复杂请求方面要好得多，尤其是当你给它详细指令或让它上网查找信息时。
在日常聊天中，你可能会注意到以下几项改进：
- 它能捕捉照片中更细微的细节，比如标签上的文字或标牌上的符号。
- 当你在网上比较各种选项时，它能更好地根据你在意的因素（比如价格或位置）来缩小范围。
- 它更懂得何时该主动提供后续服务，比如询问你是否希望在降价时收到提醒。
今天起向 Plus、Pro、Business 和 Enterprise 用户推出。
原文
We’re rolling out a version of GPT-6.2 Sol in the Chat tab, optimized for everyday conversation.
It’s much better at handling complex requests, especially when you give it detailed instructions or ask it to find information online.
A few improvements you might notice in everyday chats:
- It picks up on finer details in photos, like text on a label or symbols on a sign.
- When you’re comparing options online, it does a better job of narrowing them down based on what matters to you, like price or location.
- It has a better sense of when to offer a follow-up, like asking if you’d like a heads-up when a price drops.
Rolling out today to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.

report.summary: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT's Chat tab, tuned for everyday conversation with sharper photo reading, better online comparisons, and proactive follow-ups for paid users.
report.background: Chatbot assistants have moved through distinct phases: general-purpose chat, then multimodal (image understanding), then tool-using agents that browse the web and take follow-up actions. Most vendors now ship model variants tuned for specific surfaces rather than one static model — a fast/low-cost tier for casual chat, a heavier reasoning tier for coding and analysis. The Chat tab is the highest-volume, most consumer-facing surface, and it competes directly with Gemini, Claude, and Meta AI on everyday tasks like reading a photo of a label, comparing products, or planning a purchase. Optimizing for 'everyday conversation' means prioritizing latency, instruction-following on detailed multi-part requests, and knowing when to proactively offer a next step — a shift from answering prompts to anticipating needs. This release also signals staged, tiered rollouts, with paid subscribers getting new capabilities first.
key_points: Surface-specific tuning: this is a variant of GPT-6.2 Sol shipped specifically inside the Chat tab, not a wholesale model replacement. That pattern lets OpenAI tune latency and tone for casual conversation while keeping heavier reasoning configurations for other workloads, and it makes rollouts easier to A/B test and roll back.

Sharper multimodal detail: the model reportedly reads finer visual details such as text on a label or symbols on a sign. Practically, that means fewer misread receipts, packaging, menus, or signage — the kind of small OCR-style errors that made image chat feel unreliable for real errands.

Constraint-aware comparison: when users compare options online, it narrows results around stated priorities like price or location instead of dumping a generic list. This moves chat toward a decision-assistant role, closer to a shopping or travel agent than a search box.

Proactive follow-ups: the model has a better sense of when to offer a next step, such as asking whether you want an alert when a price drops. This is a small step toward agentic behavior — the assistant initiating actions rather than waiting to be asked.

Tiered availability: rolling out to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users only. Free-tier users are excluded at launch, keeping the strongest everyday-chat experience behind a paywall and reinforcing subscription value.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this reinforces a trend of surface-level specialization over monolithic model launches: expect more 'Chat-optimized', 'coding-optimized', and 'agent-optimized' variants, with evaluation shifting from benchmark scores to task completion in real consumer workflows. For developers, the notable signals are constraint-following on detailed instructions, reliable fine-grained image text extraction, and built-in proactivity — capabilities worth testing before building custom orchestration or OCR pipelines on top of them. For regular users, the practical gains are mundane but meaningful: reading a blurry label correctly, filtering products by what actually matters, and getting unprompted help at the right moment. The risks are equally everyday — over-eager follow-up suggestions, and a widening capability gap between paying and free users.
report.tools: To follow up: test the new Chat tab behavior directly in the ChatGPT app (Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise); benchmark alternatives via LMArena and Artificial Analysis; compare against Gemini, Claude and Meta AI on the same photo and comparison tasks. For developers evaluating image-text extraction, pair model testing with open OCR toolkits like Tesseract or PaddleOCR as a baseline, and track open-weight competitors (Llama, Qwen, Mistral) plus price-tracking APIs if you want to prototype the proactive-alert pattern yourself.
